After learning how to communicate with the animals, she struggles to fulfill her prime directive of helping others and attempts to signal the outside world for recovery. However, she soon refocuses her efforts on raising a gosling after accidentally killing its family, and makes friends with a fox named Fink (Pedro Pascal).

The Wild Robot is the last DreamWorks animated film to be animated in-house, and they went all out with it. It is incredibly stylized to capture the beauty of the natural world, while also keeping the anthropomorphization of the animals to a minimum, allowing it to depict the predator/prey relationship in a more realistic fashion compared to similar films. blocks.c: Mahito, looking at the human avatar of the heron in The Boy and The Heron

blocks.x: Following the death of his mother during the American bombing of Japan in World War II, Mahito (Luca Padovan) moves to the countryside when his father remarries his late wife's sister, Natsuko (Gemma Chan). Mahito has a difficult time adjusting to this change and even injures himself after a school fight. Over time, Mahito crosses paths with a talking Grey Heron (Robert Pattinson), who eventually lures him into an abandoned tower that transports him to a mysterious fantasy world.

The Boy and the Heron is the latest film by the great Hayao Miyazaki and has the potential to become another classic thanks to its boundless creativity and powerful themes. Along with fantastical elements like a heron who turns into a little man and fascist parakeets, the story delves into concepts like legacy, processing grief, and the pursuit of perfection. The English voice cast is made up of veterans of Studio Ghibli dubbing, but the best performances come from Pattinson, who sounds unrecognizable as the heron, and Dave Bautista, who steals the show in his limited appearance as the Parakeet King.

blocks.x: Vigilante feline hero Puss in Boots (Antonia Banderas) is disheartened to learn that he is down to his last life and, after nearly being killed by a wolf (Wagner Moura), is forced into retirement. However, Puss regains his spirit when he learns of a map that leads to a fallen star that can grant a wish. Teaming up with his old flame, Kitty Softpaws (Salma Hayek Pinault), and a small dog (Harvey Guillén), Puss delves into the Dark Forest to find the star. Along the way, he must avoid the wolf and others who want the star, like Goldilocks (Florence Pugh) and Big Jack Horner (John Mulaney).

Puss in Boots: The Last Wish exceeded all expectations for a spin-off film to become one of DreamWorks' best films. It contains mature themes of mortality, legacy, and determining what truly matters in life, but also leans into its fairy tale aesthetic, presenting its story through colorful visuals and hilarious exchanges between the characters. Speaking of the characters, each is memorable and has a plethora of quotable dialogue, especially the devious and ever-entertaining Big Jack Horner.

blocks.c: Pinocchio touching Gepetto's nose in Guillermo del Toro's Pinocchio.

blocks.x: In a drunken despair, woodcarver Geppetto (David Bradley) cuts down the tree that marks his son's grave and carves it into a puppet. When he passes out, a Wood Spirit (Tilda Swinton) decides to bring the puppet to life, naming him Pinocchio (Gregory Mann), and assigns a cricket named Sebastian (Ewan McGregor) as his conscience. As Pinocchio tries to make sense of this new world he finds himself in, many folks seek to exploit his unique abilities, such as con artist Count Volpe (Christoph Waltz) and the Podestà (Ron Perlman), who hopes to use Pinocchio as an immortal soldier loyal to Benito Mussolini (Tom Kenny).

This version of Pinocchio by the legendary dark-fantasy director Guillermo del Toro is the second stop-motion film to win the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature. It stays true to the story's origins as a cautionary tale about life's difficulties while also delving into more complex ideas like mortality, fascism, grief, and self-sacrifice. Of all the actors, Bradley is by far the standout performance of the film, especially when Geppetto is overcome with grief and despair, leading to some of the film's most heart-wrenching moments.

blocks.c: Ne Zha stands in front of water with ocean creatures and looks mischievous in Ne Zha 2.

blocks.x: As Ne Zha (Lü Yanting and Joseph Cao/Crystal Lee and Griffin Puatu) and Ao Bing (Han Mo/Aleks Le) are given new bodies by Master Taiyi Zhenren (Zhang Jiaming/Rick Zieff), dragon king Ao Guang (Li Nan and Yu Chen/Christopher Swindle), believing his son to be dead, launches an attack on Chentang Pass. This ends up destroying Ao Bing's new body, but his spirit is stored inside Ne Zha's body for the time being, and a ceasefire is declared. It turns out there is a potion that can allow Zhenren to make a new body for Ao Bing, but he and Ne Zha must complete a series of trials to become a xian.

Ne Zha 2 made history by netting over $2.270 billion, making it the highest-grossing animated film and one of the highest-grossing films of all time. One look at the animation shows why this is: the film has some of the most detailed animation ever seen, with incredibly fluid character movements and realistic fire. The story makes quite a few changes to the Chinese legend it's inspired by, but the result is still gripping, with empathetic characters and a strong message regarding destiny, balance, and the corrupting nature of power.

'The Boy and the Heron' (2023)

Image via Studio Ghibli

Following the death of his mother during the American bombing of Japan in World War II, Mahito (Luca Padovan) moves to the countryside when his father remarries his late wife's sister, Natsuko (Gemma Chan). Mahito has a difficult time adjusting to this change and even injures himself after a school fight. Over time, Mahito crosses paths with a talking Grey Heron (Robert Pattinson), who eventually lures him into an abandoned tower that transports him to a mysterious fantasy world.

The Boy and the Heron is the latest film by the great Hayao Miyazaki and has the potential to become another classic thanks to its boundless creativity and powerful themes. Along with fantastical elements like a heron who turns into a little man and fascist parakeets, the story delves into concepts like legacy, processing grief, and the pursuit of perfection. The English voice cast is made up of veterans of Studio Ghibli dubbing, but the best performances come from Pattinson, who sounds unrecognizable as the heron, and Dave Bautista, who steals the show in his limited appearance as the Parakeet King.

'Puss in Boots: The Last Wish' (2022)

Image via DreamWorks Animation

Vigilante feline hero Puss in Boots (Antonia Banderas) is disheartened to learn that he is down to his last life and, after nearly being killed by a wolf (Wagner Moura), is forced into retirement. However, Puss regains his spirit when he learns of a map that leads to a fallen star that can grant a wish. Teaming up with his old flame, Kitty Softpaws (Salma Hayek Pinault), and a small dog (Harvey Guillén), Puss delves into the Dark Forest to find the star. Along the way, he must avoid the wolf and others who want the star, like Goldilocks (Florence Pugh) and Big Jack Horner (John Mulaney).

Puss in Boots: The Last Wish exceeded all expectations for a spin-off film to become one of DreamWorks' best films. It contains mature themes of mortality, legacy, and determining what truly matters in life, but also leans into its fairy tale aesthetic, presenting its story through colorful visuals and hilarious exchanges between the characters. Speaking of the characters, each is memorable and has a plethora of quotable dialogue, especially the devious and ever-entertaining Big Jack Horner.

'Guillermo del Toro's Pinocchio' (2022)

Image via Netflix

In a drunken despair, woodcarver Geppetto (David Bradley) cuts down the tree that marks his son's grave and carves it into a puppet. When he passes out, a Wood Spirit (Tilda Swinton) decides to bring the puppet to life, naming him Pinocchio (Gregory Mann), and assigns a cricket named Sebastian (Ewan McGregor) as his conscience. As Pinocchio tries to make sense of this new world he finds himself in, many folks seek to exploit his unique abilities, such as con artist Count Volpe (Christoph Waltz) and the Podestà (Ron Perlman), who hopes to use Pinocchio as an immortal soldier loyal to Benito Mussolini (Tom Kenny).

This version of Pinocchio by the legendary dark-fantasy director Guillermo del Toro is the second stop-motion film to win the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature. It stays true to the story's origins as a cautionary tale about life's difficulties while also delving into more complex ideas like mortality, fascism, grief, and self-sacrifice. Of all the actors, Bradley is by far the standout performance of the film, especially when Geppetto is overcome with grief and despair, leading to some of the film's most heart-wrenching moments.

'Ne Zha 2' (2025)

Image via A24

As Ne Zha (Lü Yanting and Joseph Cao/Crystal Lee and Griffin Puatu) and Ao Bing (Han Mo/Aleks Le) are given new bodies by Master Taiyi Zhenren (Zhang Jiaming/Rick Zieff), dragon king Ao Guang (Li Nan and Yu Chen/Christopher Swindle), believing his son to be dead, launches an attack on Chentang Pass. This ends up destroying Ao Bing's new body, but his spirit is stored inside Ne Zha's body for the time being, and a ceasefire is declared. It turns out there is a potion that can allow Zhenren to make a new body for Ao Bing, but he and Ne Zha must complete a series of trials to become a xian.

Ne Zha 2 made history by netting over $2.270 billion, making it the highest-grossing animated film and one of the highest-grossing films of all time. One look at the animation shows why this is: the film has some of the most detailed animation ever seen, with incredibly fluid character movements and realistic fire. The story makes quite a few changes to the Chinese legend it's inspired by, but the result is still gripping, with empathetic characters and a strong message regarding destiny, balance, and the corrupting nature of power.
